dining.name: The Ivy Kensington Brasserie
dining.why: Reservation confirmed — 2, Sat Nov 7 at 8:30 AM. Veggie full English for Nicole + classic full English for Max, proper pot of tea. Kensington High St, quick hop to Harrods for 10am opening. ivycollection.com ↗

dining.name: Chez Fonfon
dining.why: Definitive bouillabaisse, Vallon des Auffes cove (since 1952) — RESERVED Sun 11/8, 8:00 PM, 2 pers (confirmation email received; bank-guarantee authorization on file). Note: window tables aren't guaranteed. Nicole: all-fish, perfect; Max: the seafood feast + wine.

dining.name: La Maison du Pastis
dining.why: Quai du Port boutique-bar with 100+ pastis & absinthes plus tastings — Max's spot to try and buy a real Marseille pastis. Pairs with panisses (fried chickpea sticks), the classic local apéritif nibble.

dining.name: Le Bar de la Marine
dining.why: Iconic Pagnol café-brasserie on the Vieux Port (15 Quai de Rive Neuve) — casual terrace, classic Marseillais plates. The Saturday-arrival pick: easy, local, and made for Max's first pastis (ask for panisses). ~10 min walk or the little César ferry across the port.

dining.name: Toinou Les Fruits de Mer
dining.why: The real Marseille oyster house at 3 Cours Saint-Louis (~8 min walk — NOT the Aix-en-Provence 'toinou.com' that looked far). Bright shellfish brasserie, open daily & late, walk-in. Arrival-night alt if you want oysters.

dining.name: Les Halles de la Major
dining.why: Waterfront food hall under the cathedral arches (Les Voûtes de la Major) — oyster bar + seafood, charcuterie & Provençal stalls. Open daily incl. Sun, casual, right on the Le Panier→MuCEM walk. Oysters for Max, seafood/veg for Nicole.

dining.name: Maison Saint Honoré
dining.why: One of Marseille's best bakeries (near Cours d'Estienne d'Orves) — superb viennoiserie, coffee & light breakfast. Casual & reliable Monday, on the way to the Rue St-Ferréol shops before the 1:04p train.

decisions.q: Menton — Plan A (with) vs Plan B (without), Wed 11/11
decisions.options: PLAN A (WITH Menton) — full Eastern-Riviera day: 9:00 train Nice→Èze cliff village; 11:00 onward to Menton (Old Town, Basilique St-Michel, Jean Cocteau museum, seafront) + lunch in Menton; ~2:00 back to Monaco (F1 circuit walk, Casino Square, afternoon Casino de Monte-Carlo + Café de Paris); 4:00 Oceanographic Museum / Prince's Palace; dinner in Monaco or Menton, or drift back to Nice whenever (trains run to ~midnight, so NO 5pm cutoff). Trade-off: busier day, earlier start; the one anchor is the ~2pm casino for the relaxed daytime dress code.  ||  PLAN B (WITHOUT Menton) — the current, calmer Monaco+Èze day: 9:00 Èze at leisure; 12:00 Café de Paris lunch; 1:00 walk the F1 circuit; 2:00 Casino de Monte-Carlo + slots; 2:30 optional Oceanographic/Prince's Palace; 7:30 dinner. Menton waits for a future trip.  ||  Note: Menton in November is quiet & charming (Lemon Festival is Feb, so nothing missed).

BASEL Great Synagogue (Leimenstrasse, 1866): interior visits are group guided tours Mon–Thu by arrangement — contact the Jewish Museum / Jewish Community of Basel to set one up (Basel weekday slots: Wed 11/18 PM arrival is tight; better a dedicated weekday). The Jewish Museum itself (Vesalgasse 5) is walk-in daily and already on 11/22.  ||  NICE Grande Synagogue (7 Rue Gustave Deloye): arrange a visit ahead (ID + security).  ||  MILAN Central Synagogue (Via Guastalla): optional guided Jewish-heritage walking tour — flexible/bookable, in addition to Binario 21 on 11/17.

options.label: Le Bar de la Marine
options.desc: Iconic Pagnol café-brasserie on the Vieux Port (15 Quai de Rive Neuve) — casual terrace, classic Marseillais plates. Perfect first-night spot for Max's pastis; ask for panisses. Open daily; ~10 min stroll or hop the little César ferry across the port.

options.label: Place de Lenche terrace (Le Panier)
options.desc: The closest + most local option — pizzas & Provençal plates on a tiny Le Panier square, ~4 min uphill from the hotel. Super casual, pastis on the terrace.

options.label: Toinou Les Fruits de Mer
options.desc: The real Marseille one at 3 Cours Saint-Louis (~8 min walk — NOT the Aix-en-Provence branch on toinou.com). Bright shellfish brasserie, open daily & late, walk-in — if you'd rather do oysters night one.

options.label: Les Halles de la Major
options.desc: Waterfront food hall under the cathedral arches (Les Voûtes de la Major) — a proper oyster bar plus seafood, charcuterie & Provençal stalls. Open daily incl. Sun, buzzy and casual, right on the Le Panier→MuCEM walk. Oysters + wine for Max; seafood/veg spread for Nicole.

options.label: Le Môle Passédat (MuCEM rooftop)
options.desc: 3-star chef Gérald Passédat's restaurant atop MuCEM with a panoramic sea & fort terrace — flows straight into your 2pm MuCEM visit. Fish-forward, scenic splurge. ⚠️ Verify Sun lunch service in Nov.

options.label: Chez Madie Les Galinettes
options.desc: Classic Provençal terrace right on Quai du Port, steps from the hotel — aïoli, grilled catch, pieds paquets for Max. ⚠️ Verify Sun opening.

options.label: Maison Saint Honoré
options.desc: One of Marseille's best bakeries (near Cours d'Estienne d'Orves) — superb viennoiserie, coffee & a light breakfast. Casual, reliable on a Monday, and on the way to the Rue St-Ferréol shops before the train.

options.label: Café de l'Abbaye (Saint-Victor)
options.desc: Terrace with a postcard view across the Vieux Port to Notre-Dame — a relaxed final-morning sit-down. ~12 min south of the hotel; leave time to get back for the 1:04p train.

options.label: Les Bords de Mer (rooftop)
options.desc: Chic seaside rooftop on the Corniche — lovely send-off, but ~20 min out; taxi back for the train.

options.label: Trattoria Masuelli San Marco
options.desc: Since 1921 — the gold-standard traditional Milanese kitchen: risotto alla milanese, ossobuco, cassoeula (in season), risotto al salto. Closed Sun + Mon lunch.

options.label: Trippa
options.desc: Milan's most celebrated modern trattoria — mondeghili, vitello tonnato, brilliant offal. Books out fast.

options.label: Trattoria Madonnina
options.desc: Home-style old Milan; the cassoeula + ossobuco spot, rustic and cozy.

options.label: Al Garghet
options.desc: One of the biggest cotolette in town + cassoeula; fireplace and garden, very November. A bit outside the center.

options.label: Al Matarel
options.desc: Brera-edge institution; 'elephant-ear' cotoletta + ossobuco falling off the bone.

options.label: Antica Trattoria della Pesa
options.desc: White-tablecloth institution on Viale Pasubio — ossobuco, cotoletta, old-Milan charm.

options.label: Berton ⭐ — business lunch
options.desc: Modern 1-star in Porta Nuova, walkable from the hotel. Weekday business lunch is the value move.

options.label: Il Luogo Aimo e Nadia ⭐
options.desc: 50-year icon, artful Italian; the lunch menu softens the price.

options.label: Sadler ⭐
options.desc: Contemporary classic on the Navigli; lunch served daily.

options.label: Skip — no Michelin this trip
options.desc: Keep it all trattoria.

options.label: Beefbar Monte-Carlo
options.desc: Sleek Monaco steak temple on the water — great for Max's meat night before the train back to Nice.

options.label: Le Bistrot d'Antoine (Nice)
options.desc: Train back to Nice and eat at the benchmark modern-Niçoise bistro in Vieux Nice.

options.label: La Merenda (Nice)
options.desc: Ex-Michelin chef's 20-seat cash-only legend; daube, stockfish. No bookings — arrive early.

options.label: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Marseille
options.desc: 16th–19th-c. painting/sculpture in the palatial Palais Longchamp; Puget, Puvis de Chavannes, a Rodin. Open Sun ✅ (closed Mon).

options.label: Musée Cantini
options.desc: Superb 1900–1980 modern art (Dufy, Derain, Kandinsky, Ernst, Miró) in a 1694 mansion. Open Sun ✅ (closed Mon).

options.label: MuCEM
options.desc: Ricciotti's lace-concrete landmark on the water; Mediterranean art/photography shows. Open Sun ✅ (closed Tue).

options.label: Musée Matisse
options.desc: ~450 works across Matisse's whole career in a red Genoese villa. Open Mon ✅ (closed Tue). Quietest month.

options.label: Musée National Marc Chagall
options.desc: The most complete Chagall on earth — 17 monumental Biblical Message canvases. Open Mon ✅ (closed Tue).

options.label: Both (Matisse + Chagall)
options.desc: Same Cimiez hill, easily combined in one afternoon — both open Monday.

options.label: MAMAC
options.desc: World-class Yves Klein room (Nice-born) + Niki de Saint Phalle, Warhol, Nouveau Réalisme. Open Wed ✅ (closed Mon).

options.label: Musée des Beaux-Arts Jules Chéret
options.desc: Monet, Renoir, Rodin, Carpeaux + Picasso ceramics in an 1878 princess's villa. Open Wed ✅ (closed Mon).

options.label: Matisse + Chagall (if skipped Mon)
options.desc: Both also open Wednesday — do Cimiez today instead if Monday fills up.

options.label: Nouveau Musée National de Monaco
options.desc: Two Belle-Époque villas, rotating modern/contemporary shows. Open Tue ✅. Only if the casino day leaves a gap.

options.label: Skip — casino day is full
options.desc: Keep Nov 11 for Èze + F1 walk + casinos.

options.label: Museo del Novecento ⭐
options.desc: 20th-c. Italian art (Futurism/Boccioni) on Piazza Duomo with Duomo views. Closed Mon (so not 11/16); FREE the 3rd Tue = Nov 17.

options.label: Pinacoteca Ambrosiana
options.desc: Caravaggio's Basket of Fruit + Leonardo's Codex Atlanticus. Closed Mon.

options.label: Museo Poldi Pezzoli
options.desc: Intimate house-museum near Brera; Pollaiuolo, Botticelli. Closed Tue (so not 11/17).

options.label: Gallerie d'Italia
options.desc: Italian 19th–20th-c. on Piazza della Scala. Closed Mon.

options.label: Peggy Guggenheim Collection ⭐
options.desc: Pollock, Picasso, Ernst, Dalí on the Grand Canal. Open Sun ✅ (closed Tue). Low Nov crowds.

options.label: Gallerie dell'Accademia
options.desc: 800 years of Venetian masters (Bellini, Titian, Tintoretto). Open Sun ✅ — CLOSED Mon 11/16, so do it today.

options.label: Punta della Dogana (Pinault)
options.desc: Bold contemporary art in Tadao Ando's restored customs house. Open Sun ✅ (closed Tue).

options.label: Palazzo Ducale (Doge's Palace)
options.desc: Tintoretto/Veronese ceilings + Bridge of Sighs. Open daily — good Mon 11/16 morning option too.

options.label: Fondation Beyeler ⭐
options.desc: One of Europe's finest — Monet, Rothko, Bacon, Giacometti in a Renzo Piano pavilion. OPEN 365 days/yr, no closures (Tram 6).

options.label: Kunstmuseum Basel
options.desc: World's oldest public art collection — Holbein to Picasso. Closed Mon (do Tue–Sun / after Strasbourg).

options.label: Museum Tinguely
options.desc: Jean Tinguely's whirring kinetic sculptures — unlike anything else. Closed Mon.

options.label: MAMC Strasbourg
options.desc: Modern & contemporary — Kandinsky, Arp, Ernst, Doré. Open Thu ✅ (closed Mon).

options.label: Skip — just wander Petite France
options.desc: Keep it a cathedral + canals stroll.

options.label: Sammlung Rosengart
options.desc: Major Picasso & Paul Klee holdings. Open Sat ✅ (winter 11:00–17:00). ⚠️ Verify at rosengart.ch — founder passed June 2026.

options.label: Skip — lake + Chapel Bridge only
options.desc: Keep the day for Old Town + optional peak.

options.label: Kunsthaus Zürich ⭐
options.desc: Switzerland's largest art museum — Giacometti, Munch, Hodler, big Impressionist holdings. Closed Mon; collection FREE on Wed (Nov 25!).

options.label: Museum Rietberg
options.desc: World-class Asian/African/Islamic/Oceanic art in park villas. Closed Mon.

options.label: Museum für Gestaltung
options.desc: Landmark graphic-design/poster collection. Closed Mon.

options.label: National Gallery of Ireland ⭐
options.desc: Caravaggio's Taking of Christ + Vermeer, Rembrandt, Yeats. FREE, open daily, Thu until 20:30 — perfect for the evening arrival.

options.label: Skip — Temple Bar + Guinness only
options.desc: Keep the short stop for a pint and the streets.

options.label: Museo Alfa Romeo (Arese) ⭐
options.desc: Official Alfa museum — GP cars, engines + trophies from the brand that won the first two F1 titles (1950 Farina, 1951 Fangio). Indoor half-day, reliable. Open daily 10–18 EXCEPT Tue → do Mon 11/16 or Fri 11/13. NW Milan (~35 min).

options.label: Autodromo Monza — track half-day
options.desc: The 'Temple of Speed' — guided pit-lane/podium tour + the 1955 banking; optional driving/hot-lap experiences (winter calendar-dependent, verify monzanet.it). ~2.5–3 hr round trip → best as a swap for the Lake Como day (Tue 11/17).

options.label: Monza town quick stop (en route to Como)
options.desc: Monza is on the Milan–Como line; hop off for the Duomo + Iron Crown of Lombardy (~10 min from the station), ~1 hr, then carry on to Como. Note: the town itself has little F1 — this is a history bonus, not the track.

options.label: Skip — Monaco F1 is enough
options.desc: Keep the F1 fix to the Monaco circuit walk + casinos on 11/11.
